title: Modine Stock Jumps 29% After Hours on Samsung Talks Report
summary: Modine stock rose over 29% after hours on a Bloomberg report that Samsung is in talks to buy the data center cooling maker. No deal has been confirmed.
body_markdown:
Rivals have been buying, too. Per Seoul Economic Daily, Vertiv bought PurgeRite for about $1 billion in December 2025, agreed to buy Thermokey in March 2026 and signed a deal for King Environmental Services in September, while Daikin bought Chilldyne and DDC Solutions in 2025.


## Modine Data Center Sales Rose 95% in Fiscal Q2


Data centers are Modine's fastest-growing business. According to the company's[results release](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-11/70027187-modine-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-results-008.htm) on Nov. 3, Data Centers segment sales rose 95% to $439.7 million from $225.0 million a year earlier, driven by higher sales to hyperscale customers in North America. The release reported these figures for the second quarter of fiscal 2027:


Metric Fiscal Q2 2027 Change vs. prior year


Net sales $994.4 million Up 35%


Data Centers segment sales $439.7 million Up 95%


Adjusted earnings per share $1.35 Up 27%


> "Data Centers and Commercial HVAC delivered strong quarters, with revenue growth of 95% and 23%, respectively."
>
>
> Neil D. Brinker, Modine CEO, in the company's results release


Modine completed the spin-off of its Performance Technologies business on Oct. 1 and now expects fiscal 2027 net sales of $3.1 billion to $3.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $470 million to $500 million, excluding that business, per the release.


## What the Samsung Talks Mean for Modine Stock


The after-hours jump came on a media report, not an announced agreement. Seoul Economic Daily reported that the shares had fallen about 15% since Modine released its[quarterly results](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) on Nov. 3, which fell short of investor expectations.


Neither company has disclosed an offer price or deal terms, and Bloomberg's sources said the talks could still collapse or draw a rival bidder, per Seoul Economic Daily.
